purpose: What the issuing bodies actually served, recorded per leg, so a pinned hash can be compared against an observation instead of against a promise.
recordedFrom: the acquire step's stdout in the job logs of the run below, read through the GitHub API
whyNotFromTheReceipts: The receipts and the acquired bytes leave the run as workflow artifacts served from productionresultssa*.blob.core.windows.net. That host answers 403 CONNECT through this session's egress proxy, and so does the storage host behind the job-log redirect and the job summary. The API's own job-log endpoint is the one transport that reaches a restricted session, which is why scripts/rcap-acquire-official-source.mjs now prints the whole receipt to stdout as well.

run.jobConclusionIsNotAnAcquisition: Every job reports success because the acquire step runs with RCAP_TOLERATE_FAILURE=1: a 404, a 403 or a transport failure is recorded and the leg exits 0 so the other forty keep their receipts. 46/46 successful jobs is not 46 acquired sources, and three of the sixteen legs read below acquired nothing.

queueAgreement.result: Every leg recorded below carries the same URL and the same expected SHA-256 in both queues, so these observations are evidence about this branch's pins. The two queues are not identical overall — the run's head had 92 master-list rows to this branch's 88, and its NC AOC-CR-298 leg names a different landing page — but no leg recorded here is affected.

coverage.whyNotAll: Each leg's log is one API call returning its full job log. Sixteen were read: every distinct outcome shape in the run, all three pattern probes, and the Priority 1 asset. The other 28 are almost all further NC legs, which share the one refusal recorded here, but they are UNREAD and nothing below should be read as covering them.

corroboratedByALaterRun.why: The run that carried the two-hop acquisition script. It is not folded into the observations above, which are the record of one run; these are the legs read from it and what they reproduce.

reproductions.result: identical a day later — 200 application/pdf, 252268 bytes, sha256 7eb2838037903de1769a0253d6ad9b092dd72f4aa363b323968c8c510fd55d3d

reproductions.andAlso: the redirect target is now recorded: https://www.vtcourts.gov/media/10142 resolves to https://www.vtcourts.gov/sites/default/files/documents/200-00132%20%E2%80%93%20Stipulation%20to%20Seal%20Criminal%20History%20Record%20%2B%20Order.pdf, confirming that VT's /media/<id> URLs are permalinks to the PDF and not landing pages. No resolution was attempted, which is the intended behaviour.

corroboratedByALaterRun.alsoConfirmed: The acquire script's receipt now reaches a restricted session: the full rcap-official-source-receipt/v2 document was read back from this run's job log, between its RCAP_RECEIPT_BEGIN/END markers, without touching the artifact host that answers 403.

whatAnObservationEstablishes: that this URL served these exact bytes to a GitHub-hosted runner at this time
whatAnObservationDoesNotEstablish: that the bytes are the current published edition
that a hash match means the pin was ever correct — it means the pin and the publisher agree today
that a 403 or 404 says anything about whether the form exists
that an unread leg behaved like a read one
